title: Protected Logical Qudits in Kitaev Quantum Double Models via Stable Representations
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires robust protection of encoded quantum information. In this work, we develop a representation-theoretic framework for constructing protected logical qudits in finite-group Kitaev quantum double models. By introducing $\varepsilon$-stable irreducible representations, we establish a necessary and sufficient existence criterion and derive ribbon--projector commutation relations that yield a $d$-dimensional protected logical subspace. We apply this construction to symmetric and alternating groups, obtaining logical qubits for $S_n$ ($n\ge 3$) and a logical qutrit for $A_4$. Moreover, the family $(\mathbb Z_2)^d\rtimes\mathbb Z_d$ realizes protected logical qudits of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. Finally, for $D(A_4)$, we describe a scheme for universal logical qutrit computation using ribbon-based logical operations.
summary: This paper develops a powerful representation-theoretic method to construct fault-tolerant logical qudits within Kitaev quantum double models. By analyzing stable representations, the authors establish existence criteria and demonstrate the realization of qudits for groups like $S_n$ and $A_4$. Ultimately, they show how these structures support universal quantum computation, advancing the theory of topological quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a representation-theoretic framework to construct and characterize protected logical qudits for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The construction successfully yields protected logical qudits for various groups, including logical qubits for $S_n$ and a logical qutrit for $A_4$, and demonstrates universal quantum computation for the $D(A_4)$ model.
method: The methodology involves using the representation theory of Kitaev quantum double models, specifically identifying $\epsilon$-stable irreducible representations to define the protected logical subspace.
model_or_system: The physical model is the Kitaev quantum double model, defined over a lattice embedded in a closed oriented surface $\Sigma$, based on a finite group $G$. The protection mechanism relies on the ground state subspace defined by local vertex and plaquette operators.
key_observables: Logical subspace dimension ($d$), logical operators ($X_L$, Hadamard), and the existence of stable representations.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the logical qudit, which is determined by the structure of the stable representations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the Kitaev quantum double model structure and the existence of specific stable representations for the chosen groups.
figures_summary: The notes mention the structure of local operators ($A_g(s), B_h(s)$) and the character tables for $A_4$ and $D(A_4)$, which characterize the underlying group structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general representation-theoretic framework for protected qudits, then applying this to specific groups ($S_n, A_4$), and finally demonstrating universal quantum computation using the $D(A_4)$ structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical link between abstract group theory (representation theory) and the physical realization of robust quantum information storage and computation, which is fundamental to quantum computing theory.
